title: Toilets, waste and hygiene when the water stops
short: A toilet without water, clean hands, rubbish
intro: Readings for when the toilet cannot be flushed or the water is off: a substitute toilet, keeping hands clean, and rubbish. The library has only short passages on this; what is missing is listed below.

choices.label: The toilet can't be flushed
choices.hint: No water, a long blackout, damaged sewers

read.label: A makeshift toilet: a bag on a bucket
read.note: In Polish. From the government's safety guide: without running water, put a plastic bag on a bucket, throw it into a separate container after use, and cover the smell with soil, sawdust or cat litter.

read.label: Strong bags to hang in the toilet
read.note: In German. The hygiene checklist: large, sturdy bin bags for the toilet, a camping toilet, and other hygiene items.

read.label: A substitute toilet if water or sewers fail
read.note: In German. Part of the first steps at home in a blackout.

read.label: How much water a flush uses
read.note: Up to 7 litres each time; simpler toilets need far less. Written for relief planners.

choices.label: Keep hands clean with little water
choices.hint: No running water, soap running out

read.label: When and how long to wash your hands
read.note: WHO advice: wash with soap before and while handling food and after the toilet, for 40–60 seconds, or rub with an alcohol hand rub for 20–30 seconds.

read.label: Clean hands before touching drinking water
read.note: Washing hands before handling stored water, and a tap on the container.

read.label: Gloves, disposable plates and cutlery
read.note: In German. Dishes cannot be washed without water and power; gloves help when you must dress a wound and cannot wash your hands.

choices.label: Rubbish is piling up
choices.hint: No collection, food waste, smells, flies

read.label: Keep rubbish sealed
read.note: WHO advice after floods: keep waste in sealed bins and food in sealed containers, out of reach of rats.

read.label: Avoid waste and collect it in bags

choices.label: Drains after a flood, or sewage backing up
choices.hint: Flooded cellar, backed-up drains, a sewage pump

read.label: Before you use the drains after a flood
read.note: In Italian. Find out whether sewers, septic tanks and wells are damaged, and follow the authorities before cleaning up.

read.label: Sewage pumps and backflow valves
read.note: In German. If the house has its own sewage pump, check it and any backflow valves.

limits.text: Rubbish and excrement left lying around breed insects and disease within a few days.
After a flood, find out whether sewers, septic tanks and wells are damaged before you use the drains.
In a long blackout, washing comes second: drinking water must be saved.

prepare.label: What households forget: toilet paper, bags, gloves
